title: ‘End of Oak Street’ Box Office Aims to Take Bite Out of ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All August 12, 2026 5:41pm Ewan McGregor (left) and Anne Hathaway in 'The End of Oak Street.' Courtesy Warner Bros. Pictures Logo text It’s dinosaur mayhem at the box office as two newcomers about the prehistoric beasts — The End of Oak Street and PAW Patrol : The Dino Movie — set out to challenge the behemoth that is Spider-Man : Brand New Da y. Warner Bros. releases director David Robert Mitchell’s The End of Oak Street in 3,400 North American theaters on Friday, with the studio projecting an opening weekend in the range of $18 million to $23 million. Warner Bros. expects to add between $20 million to $25 million internationally for the sci-fi survival movie that hails from Bad Robot and carries an $80 million production budget. Related Stories Movies A Movie Theater Didn't Get Sent 'Spider-Man' Posters, So an Employee Drew His Own Movies X-Men: All the Actors Lobbying to Play Marvel's Mutants Anne Hathaway continues her busy 2026 , leading the cast that also includes Ewan McGregor , Maisy Stella and Christian Convery. Mitchell, known for the 2014 horror hit It Follows , helmed the movie from his own script about a family in the early 1980s as they realize that their suburban neighborhood has been transported to an area with prehistoric predators. The End of Oak Street holds an 82 percent approval rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter , chief film critic David Rooney called the movie “mindlessly entertaining in a big-dumb-fun kind of way.” At the Oak Street premiere, Hathaway expressed to THR her gratitude “that audiences want to go see original things, and this movie is really original.” PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie Paramount Pictures /Courtesy Everett Collection For those seeking a more family-friendly dino adventure, Paramount Pictures releases PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie in more than 3,500 locations in North America. For the third feature installment in producer Spin Master Entertainment’s animated franchise, the studio projects a domestic opening ranging in the mid-to-high teens after having already surpassed $27 million in 30 international markets. Dino Movie has a $39.5 million production budget. Carter Young, Mckenna Grace , Terry Crews, Jennifer Hudson and Snoop Dogg are among the voice stars for director Cal Brunker’s film that sees our Paw Patrol canine heroes end up in a world containing dinosaurs. The previous sequel, 2023’s PAW Patrol: The Mighty Movie , opened to $22.7 million domestically in late September. Its $205 million global run improved upon the $144 worldwide total for 2021’s original PAW Patrol: The Movie , which adapted the series that first launched on Nick Jr. in 2013. The release of a PAW Patrol movie can be counted on to increase interest in all iterations of the brand, including merchandise and streaming for the shows. PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie has earned an 85 percent critics score on Rotten Tomatoes, with THR critic Frank Scheck writing that, “while the material is thoroughly juvenile, the films impart valuable messages to their impressionable viewers.” Meanwhile, Spider-Man: Brand New Day will continue flying high with its third straight weekend at the top of the box office chart. Sony Pictures expects filmmaker Destin Daniel Cretton’s smash hit to bring its domestic total to $700 million in the next day or so as the film looks to soon surpass the global sum of $1.9 billion that previous franchise title Spider-Man: No Way Home collected after opening in December 2021. Starring Tom Holland , Zendaya and Sadie Sink , Brand New Day has notched no shortage of records in its historic run. Thanks to hits like Brand New Day , The Odyssey , Toy Story 5 and others, the summer box office surpassed the $4 billion mark this week, representing just the second time that the prime moviegoing season has achieved this since the COVID pandemic. (The first time was 2023, aka the summer of Barbenheimer.) This means that the all-time summer mark of $4.755 billion from 2013 could still remain within reach. Other new theatrical options this weekend include thriller The Rivals of Amziah King , starring Matthew McConaughey , and the Kristen Stewart -led stoner comedy The Wrong Girls . THR

title: California Pressured By Two Hollywood Unions to Settle Paramount-Warner Bros. Lawsuit
full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All August 12, 2026 5:36pm California attorney general Rob Bonta. Eric Lee/Getty Images Logo text Two top Hollywood unions are calling for California attorney general Rob Bonta and Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison to reach a settlement on their pending antitrust case because, they argue, industry workers are being harmed by the delayed timeline. The leaders of the Directors Guild of America and IATSE made the request on Thursday in a letter that claimed their members are already seeing productions being put on hold or canceled as the two companies prepare for a March 2027 antitrust trial . Against a backdrop of already scant work, particularly in the L.A. area, DGA national executive director Russell Hollander and IATSE international president Matthew Loeb argued that the consequences of additional uncertainty would be borne by the rank and file. “We write to raise concerns about the potential for a prolonged timetable for the litigation… and express to you the importance that you engage directly with each other to negotiate a resolution that ameliorates the anti-competitive aspects of the proposed merger,” their letter stated. “Should such an agreement prove impossible, we would ask that both parties seek to move the start of the trial to an earlier date, as continued delay and uncertainty around the future of WBD only harms our members.” The leaders of the unions, which together represent roughly 200,000 workers in the entertainment business, conceded that in the past mergers have offered “few benefits” to workers. Still, “While we continue to have significant concerns about the proposed merger, we believe many of these concerns can be addressed through the imposition of enforceable conditions in a binding agreement,” the letter stated. Suggested conditions include keeping Paramount and Warner Bros. operating as entirely separate film and television studios and remaining sellers in the marketplace. Hollander and Loeb also suggest that the combined company could commit to producing projects in the U.S. “at no less than the average percentage produced in the United States during the past five years” and to keeping Paramount based in Los Angeles, among other suggested provisions. The letter puts the two unions at odds with their colleagues at the Writers Guild of America, a labor group that has been vociferously opposed to the $111 billion mega-merger and sued to block the deal itself . The performers’ union SAG-AFTRA has also opposed the deal unless “enforceable safeguards” are put in place. The Teamsters union previously called for the Department of Justice to block the deal (which it did not do) unless worker protections are instituted. The objective with their approach, said the two unions’ leaders, was to mitigate harm to their members. “Our goal, with respect to the proposed merger, has always been to achieve an outcome that ensures a vibrant, competitive marketplace for the production, distribution, and licensing of film and television programming that serves the interests of consumers and filmmakers alike,” the labor leaders stated. “We believe that these conditions, if secured through a binding agreement, will largely serve this purpose.” Read the full letter below. title: StubHub Is Spending Millions Trying to Stop a Bill That Would Cap Concert Ticket Resale Prices
full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All August 12, 2026 4:57pm A Stubhub banner hangs at the New York Stock Exchange as the company prepares to ring the opening bell on September 17, 2025 in New York City. Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images StubHub ’s lobbying expenses have reached an all-time high in California, as the ticket resale platform has spent millions of dollars over the past few months looking to stop a bill that seeks to place limits on how much concert tickets are allowed to sell for on resale services in the Golden State. The company reported nearly $2.6 million in lobbying expenses in California from April to June, per filings reviewed by The Hollywood Reporter. According to the Capitol Morning Report, that makes StubHub the second-largest lobbying spender in the state for the quarter, behind only Pacific Gas & Electric and ahead of the likes of Chevron, Verizon, AT&T and OpenAI, among others. It’s the most StubHub has ever spent on lobbying in any quarter in California, per publicly available documents. Overall, StubHub has spent $3.4 million this calendar year. The company’s record spending follows AB 1720, a bill from state assembly member Matt Haney introduced in February that, if passed, would limit concert ticket resale prices to no more than 10 percent higher than a ticket’s original price. Since its introduction, the bill already has been abated with an amendment limiting the law only to smaller 3,000-capacity venues or lower, removing most of the major amphitheater, arena and stadium dates that usually draw much of the activity on secondary ticketing sites. When asked for comment, StubHub said the platform “exists to give fans access to live events on their own terms through a secure, verified marketplace — including fans who couldn’t get tickets during the original on-sale, or who want the option of grabbing a great deal as prices shift closer to the event.” “We believe that more choice, flexibility, and access put fans first and help everyone get into the events they love,” StubHub said. AB 1720 received support from groups representing artists and indie venues including the National Independent Venue Association, the Future of Music Coalition and the Music Artist Coalition. It’s also drawn support from live music giant Live Nation Entertainment, owner of the eponymous concert promoter and the oft-bemoaned Ticketmaster, the primary ticketing provider for most of the major concert venues in the U.S. Proponents for price caps argue adding a hard limit on secondary ticketing would be a major step in ending ticket scalping, as brokers would no longer be allowed to list tickets at extreme markups, and thus their profit motive would be taken away. Price cap bills have begun picking up steam over the past several years, particularly as long-held fan outrage over concert ticket prices has grown louder in the 2020s. California isn’t the only state that’s considered price caps this year. Maine, Vermont and Washington, D.C . all passed price cap laws in recent months, and Massachusetts governor Maura Healey announced in July that she was placing a price cap law for review in the state’s supplemental spending bill. Noah Kahan was one of dozens of New England acts who voiced his support for the Massachusetts bill, and he appeared over video during Healey’s press conference announcing the law. He also helped get a price cap bill passed in his home state of Vermont. “The artist community and fans greatly benefit from limiting ticket scalping,” Kahan said last month. “I love my fans and I want to protect them however I can. Artists alone could not tackle the market manipulation of secondary resellers.” During a press conference on Tuesday, Haney, the state assemblymember who introduced AB 1720, said that “right now, fans are getting ripped off.” “Today, professional scalpers have turned it into a massive multi-billion-dollar business,” Haney said. “They buy up tickets as soon as they go on sale, not because they want to go to the show, but because they know you want to go to the show. Then they charge you two, three, four, sometimes five times’ what they paid for. Then regular fans are left with a choice: pay hundreds of dollars more to go, or don’t go at all.” Price caps overall, though, have received significant pushback from ticket brokers and resale platforms like StubHub, SeatGeek and Vivid Seats. (SeatGeek and Vivid Seats both reported significantly smaller lobbying expenses, as SeatGeek has spent about $40,000 this year, while Vivid Seats reported $500). Financially, caps represent a potential hurdle for their revenue streams, as their business models are built on collecting fees attached to ticket sales, and those fee amounts depend on a ticket’s sales price. Both StubHub and Vivid Seats mention price caps in their risk factors to their businesses in their most recent 10-K reports. Stephen Parker, the executive director of the National Independent Venue Association, a supporter of 1720, called StubHub’s lobbying spending on the bill an act of “desperation.” “They are staring into a future that does not allow them to make millions across the entire sector by price gouging consumers across the country,” Parker says. “California is one of the biggest concert markets in the country. If California goes in terms of consumer protections around ticketing, we think the rest of the nation will soon follow.” Parker also turned attention toward StubHub CEO Eric Baker, who’d drawn backlash last month over revelations that he also runs Andro Capital, a hedge fund that funds ticket brokers who sell tickets on the platform. House Democrats announced a probe into StubHub in July, and both Baker and the company were hit with a class action suit over claims of fraudulent misrepresentation and violation of state consumer protection statutes. (In a statement on the matter, a StubHub rep said that Baker’s affiliation with the fund was listed publicly, and that “This relationship with Andro Capital makes up only a small fraction of StubHub’s total revenue.”) “Their CEO is not just a platform operator, he’s also funding scalpers,” Parker says. “They have a lot to lose.” Much of StubHub’s lobbying expenses this quarter has gone to the Ticket Policy Forum, a coalition that represents StubHub and other resale platforms including SeatGeek, Vivid Seats and TickPick. StubHub paid Ticket Policy Forum over $1 million this quarter, and the organization’s work has included mail ads calling for voters to tell their representatives to vote no 1720, describing the bill as a Live Nation-Ticketmaster initiative to exact more control over the market. In an email, Ticket Policy Forum executive director Brian Berry further stated that the bill only further empowers Ticketmaster because it places caps only on resale and doesn’t address rising ticket prices on the primary side as well. “Exempting Ticketmaster from price controls will not result in lower ticket prices since the illegal monopoly often secretly holds back ticket inventory to create artificial scarcity to support higher prices, and uses dynamic and platinum pricing to arbitrarily raise ticket prices while tickets are on sale,” Berry said. “Capping only resale does nothing to address this source of rising ticket prices. AB 1720 would let the Live Nation-Ticketmaster monopoly keep raising costs unchecked while jeopardizing the benefits fans stand to gain as remedies are decided in the ongoing Live Nation-Ticketmaster antitrust case. Legislation that fosters open, fair and safe competition, improves transparency and fights fraud and deception is more effective and should be made a priority.” As Berry says, scalpers on the secondary market aren’t the only problem in the concert business. Prices continue to grow higher on the primary side as well, and dynamic pricing and higher fees are two of concertgoers’ most frequent complaints about purchasing tickets. Fans have hated Ticketmaster for years, and back in April, Live Nation lost its antitrust lawsuit , with a jury determining the company operates as a monopoly. Live Nation-Ticketmaster’s support has led to skepticism toward the bill — the company has reported about $91,000 in lobbying in 2026 in California — though 1720 has also drawn support from groups that have been particularly vocal in advocating for a Live Nation breakup, such as NIVA and the Future of Music Coalition. Kevin Erickson, the Future of Music Coalition’s executive director, calls framing price caps as a Ticketmaster-friendly measure “dishonest,” adding that a better ecosystem requires reform on both the primary and secondary marketplaces, and that they aren’t mutually exclusive. “The behaviors [secondary platforms] have been engaging in and the practices that have become core to their business model are indefensible,” Erickson says. “The point isn’t to get rid of the secondary market but to create a system that aligns with the needs of fans, ticket buyers as well as artists and presenters. What we’re advocating for is the ability for artists to charge less than what the market could theoretically bear, and they can’t control that when scalpers use that dynamic to profit. Why accept this impoverished version of the music business where it’s just a cash grab above everything else? When we accept that level of cynicism, we’ve lost a whole lot of what makes live music special.” THR

title: ‘Wizards of Waverly Place’ Actress Jennifer Stone, Who Now Works as a Nurse, Says She Auditioned for ‘The Pitt’

Like, I started having to like talk myself down.” “I have a hard time watching it ’cause it’s too close to home a little bit,” Stone added of The Pitt . title: A Movie Theater Didn’t Get Sent ‘Spider-Man’ Posters, So an Employee Drew His Own
full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 12, 2026 3:54pm The viral Canadian 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' poster, and the movie's official movie poster. Drake Landon; Columbia Pictures Logo text The promotional materials for Spider-Man : Brand New Day look a bit different in one theater in Canada, and the internet is loving it. A Famous Players theater in Prince George, British Columbia almost certainly has the most unique movie poster for the record-breaking film led by Tom Holland. It features a hand-drawn illustration by employee Drake Landon that was inspired by the Spooder-Man meme , with the title of the movie written in font strikingly similar to the script in the official promotional materials. The movie theater did not receive the official movie poster in time for its release, which led to Landon creating an original drawing to be put in its place in the cinema. That was explained in his now-viral illustration, as a note on the poster reads, “Sorry! We never recieved the real posters! Sorry for any inconviniences!” (Yes, with those exact spelling errors and all, adding to the amusement surrounding the sketch.) Related Stories Movies Frank Miller Talks Arguing with Jim Shooter, Why His Doctor Strange Series Never Happened and 'Sin City' Future Business Cineplex CEO Says Gen Z Is Ready to Go to the Movies: "They're Tired of Looking at Small Screens" Pictures of the poster have gained widespread attention online, with one Reddit post receiving upwards of 51,000 upvotes. Landon tells The Hollywood Reporter the reaction to his Spider-Man poster has been “very unexpected,” and he’s “kinda still not realizing how big it is.” ‘ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ‘ illustration by Drake Landon. Drake Landon Landon adds, “It’s crazy that my art has gone that far for something so simple.” He also confirms that “the inspiration for it was the ‘Spooder-man’ meme that was popular around in the 2010s.” Michelle Saba, vp of communications for Cineplex , owner of Famous Players, also commended the poster in a statement shared with THR . “Our team did have a little fun as they awaited the arrival of their Spider-Man: Brand New Day poster,” she said. It’s no secret that Spider-Man: Brand New Day has been a smash hit — at the box office , and with viewers. The film triumphed over many records originally set by Avengers: Endgame , including by earning the highest-grossing first week in domestic box office history and becoming the fastest title to reach $500 million domestic. Brand New Day hit that milestone in its first seven days; Endgame hit the threshold in eight days. The movie also earned the best-ever domestic box office sums for a Monday and a Tuesday ; is the second-fastest film to achieve $1 billion globally ; and scored the third-best second weekend ever at the box office. Spider-Man related content is hotter than ever, and Famous Players’ viral hand-drawn poster for the film is another piece of media that has proved just that. A Facebook post made by a moviegoer who attended the Canadian theater also shared a photo of the artist, Landon, posing by his now-viral masterpiece. “My son Rogan and I stopped to appreciate this hand drawn movie poster at the theatre today and thought it was awesome. Then we got a chance to meet the artist, Drake. So my son decided to take a picture of the artist with his art work and we thought we should share it for everyone to check out,” wrote Adam Woodrow. “Keep it up Drake!” Cineplex CEO Ellis Jacob commended Gen Z for driving the recent success at the box office in a recent interview with THR . “The big change is Gen Z are coming back to the movies in a big way, and that’s making a difference,” he said. “They’re tired of looking at the small screen. They’re going out on a social basis and having a good time and that to me is very positive.” THR

full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten , Jill Goldsmith , Tom Tapp August 12, 2026 7:55am Bob Iger Getty UPDATED with Magic Johnson comments: Fulfilling a long-held dream, Bob Iger has bought himself a big-city major sports franchise. The ex- Disney CEO and Thrive Capital boss Josh Kushner have scored the Los Angeles Lakers at a valuation of $12.5 billion, Deadline has confirmed. That’s the highest valuation for a sports team in U.S. history, topping the record set when current owner owner Mark Walter bought the team just over one year ago. They will be buying out Walter’s 80% stake in the team. Related Stories Sports LeBron James Signs With Philadelphia 76ers As “Last Decision”: “I Am So Excited To Energize A New Fan Base” Sports Donald Trump Says LeBron James Is “Maybe A Racist” After 76ers Move & Prefers Michael Jordan: “I Only Like People Who Like Me” “As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honored for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world,” Iger and Kushner said in a statement Wednesday. “We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss. Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans and the city of Los Angeles.” Of interest to longtime fans is the fate of Jeanie Buss, who under and agreement with Walter is serving as the team’s governor in league meetings. Watch on Deadline “We have enormous respect and appreciation for Jeanie, her father and what they’ve contributed to this franchise,” Iger told The California Post . “And we have every intention to honor the agreement that was made between Mark and Jeanie. If things change, they’ll change, but we’re going into this with enormous respect and appreciation for who she is and what she represents in the organization.” Even as the deal needs to get formal thumbs-up from the NBA Board of Governors, Iger and Kushner got the stamp of approval from Lakers legend Magic Johnson ASAP. “Laker fans, you couldn’t have two better owners,” Johnson posted online this morning. “I’ve known Bob personally for over 40 years — he has always loved the Lakers and basketball, and he will bring championships back to LA” I want to congratulate my good friend Bob Iger and Josh Kushner on their purchase of the Los Angeles Lakers! — Earvin Magic Johnson (@MagicJohnson) August 12, 2026 Laker fans, you couldn’t have two better owners. I’ve known Bob personally for over 40 years – he has always loved the Lakers and basketball and he will bring championships back to LA. — Earvin Magic Johnson (@MagicJohnson) August 12, 2026 The team’s current superstar, Luka Doncic, who was traded to the Lakers in a deal that blindsided not just the league, but Doncic as well, said in part, “I’ve gotten used to big changes over these last few years, but I know that no matter what, there is no limit to the potential of this iconic franchise. I look forward to meeting Josh and Bob so we can get to work building something special in LA together.” Lakers minority owner and current governor Jeanie Buss retweeted Doncic and wrote, “Perfectly said,” alongside gold and purple hear emojis. Perfectly said 💛💜 https://t.co/f7GL4tbG8n — Jeanie Buss (@JeanieBuss) August 12, 2026 After two stints as Disney boss, Iger exited the CEO seat in March. He rejoined Thrive as an adviser in April, setting the table for today’s big news. It has been a true whirlwind for the 17-time NBA champion Lakers the past year — and we’re not just talking about LeBron James leaving and joining the 76ers . There was the Doncic deal, the sale of the team to Walter last year and now this. And “this” came together in just three days. Los Angeles Lakers players Jake LaRavia, left, and Luka Doncic in 2025 Iger has talked for years about owning a major sports franchise. He and Kushner had been part of a group exploring an NBA expansion franchise in Las Vegas. Iger told the Post in an interview today, “We were involved in pursuing the new franchise in Vegas. And while that happened, it was suggested to us that maybe Mark Walter would be interested in selling his stake in the Lakers. And we immediately decided that given the value of the franchise and the iconic nature of the team, that we would be really smart to pursue it. The deal came together in three days.” Angel City FC stakeholder Iger and Kushner, the once-FIFA-touted financial player (and Donald Trump family member by marriage), take a controlling interest in the one-time home of Magic, Shaq and Kobe from Mark Walter about a year after the Guggenheim Partners CEO bought the Lakers from the Buss family at a valuation of $10 billion . While Walter got close to 80% of the franchise, the the Buss family trust retained a 15% interest. According to The Athletic , Kushner owns a minority stake in the Miami Heat, which he will likely have to divest. League rules specify that no one can own interest in more than one team. Given the soaring cost of franchises, NBA owners in 2024 voted to allow private equity groups to buy minority stakes in multiple teams, but not a controlling interest. Kushner also once owned a minority strake in the Memphis Grizzlies. He started Thrive Capital in 2009 with backing from Peter Thiel, according to The Athletic. Iger came on as a minority investor in 2022. Earlier this year, Thrive Capital launched a holding company called Thrive Eternal, whose investments, said Kushner, would be in “iconic franchises and cultural institutions rooted in tradition, identity, and shared experience.” The holding company is, according to The Athletic , the vehicle by which Kushner and Iger intend to buy the Lakers. Thrive Eternal was one of the investors in the controversial recent plan by FIFA president Gianni Infantino to create a $20 billion commercial arm of soccer’s world governing body by selling stakes in the World Cup and other events. That plan was scuttled after widespread outcry in the soccer world and beyond.
